sessions.title: PG's Playhouse: The Evolution of Escape Rooms
sessions.description:
Escape rooms have come a long way from the days of being locked in a room filled with padlocks and riddles. These live action, site-specific adventures are defying genres by cross pollinating with immersive theater, haunts, board games, and video games.

We start off with a PG's Playhouse style puzzle game that's a mashup of wordplay and trivia, and then we'll explore the evolution of escape rooms.

sessions.title: Night Market
sessions.description:
Sell, barter, swap, loan, and give away your indie board games, puzzles, collector's items, and whatever else you wish!

Want to run a booth at Night Market? Apply for one here: https://bit.ly/metagame-night-market

sessions.title: The Interface Is The Game
sessions.description: An interface is just one part of a game, but the player's opinion and experience with a game can hinge entirely on the interface. Sirlin shares several anecdotes where interfaces either shaped perception of his games or even drove the entire game's design. This talk applies to tabletop games as well as video games.

sessions.title: Escape Room Session 1
sessions.description: On Saturday, a team of 10-20 amateur escape room architects built an escape room in 5 hours. Now, you have 30 minutes to play that escape room. Slots for 4-8 players will be available all day Sunday for conference attendees to play, with the escape room architects making tweaks as gameplay evolves.

sessions.title: Red Teaming Rules Design
sessions.description: Have you ever looked through a board game rulebook, gotten annoyed that it doesn't answer your question, and thought to yourself "I could do a better job"? Well, now is your chance to find out! Join us as we apply some computer security principles to reverse-engineer a small part of the Magic: The Gathering rulebook, and learn just how much goes into writing robust game rulesets. (No prior Magic knowledge required.)

sessions.title: Will Shortz Q&A
sessions.description: Will Shortz himself, the enigmatology major who has been New York Times puzzle editor since 1993, is making a virtual appearance! Come prepared to solve a word puzzle or ask him an interesting question about anything.

sessions.title: Pitch Your Pet Game!
sessions.description:
Running something cool this weekend? Want people to learn why it's the best thing ever? Come pitch your thing in a 3 minutes or less.
Let folks know any constraints (e.g. running it all day Saturday but not Sunday, not appropriate for children, requires at least 6 players, takes 2+ hours, etc) that might be relevant. This doesn't have to be just homemade games, it can be anything you want to schedule/run.

sessions.title: Blood on the Clocktower
sessions.description:
It's the best Werewolf/Mafia game ever made! 
Find and kill the Demon lurking among you before the secret evil players destroy the town. Even if you are killed, you still play on as a ghost.

I've run almost 1000 new players through this game.

sessions.title: Rules Are A Cage
sessions.description: Rules are, in many ways, the fundamental building blocks of the games we play. But what even are they, and how do they shape the games we play? Join award-winning game designer Jay Dragon as she works through the particular oddities of rules, across board games, TTRPGs, LARPs, videogames, and playground games.

sessions.title: Build your own Escape Room
sessions.description:
In this hands-on workshop, we’ll see just how quickly we can build one together. You’ll team up to create puzzles, props, and lore for a brand-new escape room and the very next day, you’ll get to watch people try (and maybe fail) to escape the room you helped design!
We’ll kick off with a 20-minute intro + brainstorm, then dive straight into designing and building. No experience required! Whether it’s your very first time or you’re a seasoned escape room maker, this is your chance to see what you can create with a group in under 3 hours.

sessions.title: Beautiful Suffering: How I Created a Larp to Drive People Insane
sessions.description: Fielding's Hollow is a Gilded Age larp for 16 players about betrayal, drugs, and Gnosticism that runs every autumn in a secret location in New England. You can only play it once in your life. In this talk I'll discuss my approach to creating the game, how it aligns with my personal spiritual practice, and what it takes to make people feel like they're going a little bit insane.

sessions.title: Playtesting and Game Design at Cards Against Humanity
sessions.description: I'll talk about playtesting and game design process at at Cards Against Humanity. How do we pick which cards go in the game? What principles guide the design of new games and new twists on our original? What even makes a comedy party game work?

sessions.title: So You Wanna Make a Tabletop Game: Designing for Mass Production and Working with Manufacturers
sessions.description: How do you create a custom die cut? What's the difference between a resin mold and a PVC mold? How do you find manufacturing partners and ask for quotes? What about file preparation? What's an MOQ? All these questions and more will be answered in this basic crash course on designing for manufacturing.

sessions.title: Wait, you're NOT an escape room enthusiast?!
sessions.description: You love gaming. You're passionate about immersive entertainment. But you don't like escape rooms?! Summer explores the disconnect she often encounters when talking with people about escape rooms and how to turn someone - maybe even you! - from a doubter into an escape room convert.

sessions.title: The Exquisite Corpse Factory
sessions.description:
Extremelyl friendly to spectators! Possibly friendly to people joining mid-game!

The Exquisite Corpse Factory is set at a factory where new and unfamiliar illustrations of weird monsters are constructed. 

This prototype by Jay Dragon was created in the past week!

sessions.title: Suspicious Pile of Rocks: Letterboxing and the Search for Hidden Treasure
sessions.description: Letterboxing is a real-life treasure hunt in which participants follow clues to find hidden boxes, each containing a hand-carved rubber stamp and a logbook. Since first discovering this underground hobby at age 12, Matthew has found over 6,000 letterboxes all over the world and created hundreds of his own, providing a vast library of site-specific experience design practices that unknowingly set the stage for his later career as a puzzle and ARG designer. Diving deep down the rabbit hole of letterboxing, this talk will also touch on stamp passports, public art exchanges, puzzles for non-puzzlers, and best practices for boldly hiding secrets in plain sight.

sessions.title: Play This Talk
sessions.description: Playing games is fun, and learning is fun, so learning is play, is something you might conclude if you never learned about false syllogisms. However you can indeed learn things by playing games, and if you play enough games with enough people over enough time, you might learn enough stuff to put it together into a talk that is also, oddly, a game that the presenter plays by, for, with, and at times against the audience. And if you don't do that, it's OK, nobody else has either, making tonight's presenter the first. Perhaps there's a reason for that. We'll find out together. Along the way, we'll have some fun and discuss Survivor challenges, balloon manipulation, gender as a societal construct, and topographical neuroscience.

According to Bernard Suits, they are the only possible source of meaning in a world without want. But what do they mean for us, here, in Berkeley, in 2025, somewhere between pre-history and utopia?

The viral daily biology game Metazooa comes to life in an immersive outdoor experience! Come to the Gardens to meet Abe, the founder of the indie game studio Trainwreck Labs, for the official kickoff of this weekend-long, nature-themed scavenger hunt. 

Learn more about the event here
https://metazooa.live

.

sessions.title: FATHERFOG, the Fairytale Horror RPG
sessions.description: FATHERFOG, the Fairytale Horror TTRPG, is the next game from the team that brought you MOTHERSHIP, the sci-fi horror rpg. Fairy tales exist in a world covered in a thick fog. Can you survive?

sessions.title: This Talk Will Not Be Boring (And Neither Should Anything Else)
sessions.description: Every day, people encounter mandatory friction: overcomplicated instructions, error messages, complex signage, long, rambling talk descriptions, all of which drain our souls. But Jordan Gold and Tommy Honton are here to question it all and ask, “How can this feel better?” What if those universal moments of slowness and boredom could become, dare we say, unexpected moments of delight? What if our most frustrating touchpoints are actually our greatest opportunities for connection and joy? If you're still reading this, you're already in, right?

sessions.title: LLMing Together A Playable Roguelike In A Month
sessions.description:
For the first-time we have non-human intelligence to work with, and yet we don't have a generation of games using it as a core mechanic. Let's be the change we want to see in the world: Patrick presents an art project, a fantasy-themed roguelike, which he designed and coded (using LLMs, naturally) in under a month. It uses LLMs as a core game mechanic and for story and asset generation.

Attendees at Metagame can play this with Megagame integration during and after the talk!

sessions.description: I am fascinated by the art and craft of collaboration, and have its practice and the study of how and why collaboration works at the center of my professional career as an entrepreneur, a software architect, as well as a creator, producer & publisher in the game industry. I seek to understand what makes creating together powerful and joyful. Drawing on my work with Tableau (a story game), Meeples Together (book on cooperative tabletop design), and Polis Play (playful experiments with collaborative governance), this session will highlight emerging “patterns” of collaborative play and invite participants to workshop new ones.

sessions.title: Crossword Relay Race Intro
sessions.description:
Players on the Orange and Purple teams will compete to construct a crossword in pairs that separately construct the theme, grid, fill, and clues without further coordination between them. This session is an introduction explaining the rules of the Crossword Construction Relay Race and starting the clock on constructions. The event will be judged by speedsolvers who race to complete those crosswords and select their favorite on Sunday morning.

This session is part of the Megagame.

sessions.title: Blood on the Clocktower
sessions.description:
It's the best Werewolf/Mafia game ever made! 

If this is overbooked, I will prioritize new players!

sessions.title: Jubensha: Tree Rings Murder Mystery
sessions.description: Try the hit murder mystery genre from China, and see what all the fuss is about. In Tree Rings, you're a suspect in a bizarre, supernatural murder. Or this might be a 2-hour prototype playtest, we haven't figured out which yet. Part TTRPG, part LARP, part multimedia performance. Can you figure out who the murder is, and survive? Available for the first time in English.

sessions.description:
David Sirlin is bringing these playtest games and they'll be set up all day in this room, with Sirlin and helpers constantly starting new sessions!
Games:

--Tak variant. Abstract strategy game. (2p, 30m)
--Hungry Hungry Pandas. Party game. (Up to 8p)

sessions.title: Puzzle design challenges from Patrick's Parabox
sessions.description: This talk covers some unique design challenges encountered and solved during the development of Patrick's Parabox, an award-winning puzzle game with recursive mechanics released on Steam in 2022. It covers how the ruleset evolved over the years, how level design was refined, iterating based on playtesting, and some unique programming. And a design philosophy of optimizing the presentation of a core mechanic and surfacing joyful moments to players.

sessions.title: Taser Duels
sessions.description: Step into the arena where the stakes are high and the blades are live. Armed with electrified knives, Orange and Purple champions face off in a series of 1-on-1 duels. Each strike delivers a shock and brings their team closer to victory. Three clean hits wins the round; best of 3 rounds decides the match. Expect cheers, shocks, and glory — the air will be electric… and so will the knives.

sessions.title: Crossword Speedsolving, Judging, and Live Editing
sessions.description:
Multiple crossword speedsolving recordholders will compete to finish the crosswords that the Orange and Purple constructed on Saturday. Then, they'll judge the results. All are welcome to spectate or speedsolve alongside them.  

Once that's wrapped, we'll do some live editing together! See you soon :)

sessions.title: Election Tournament Debate
sessions.description:
Which box are you going to drop your vote token in? Come decide at this dramatic live debate featuring the nominees for Sovereign of Metagame. You will have the opportunity to ask questions to the candidates! There may be a twist...

NOTE: If you want to have a chance to compete in the debate and election, come to Stage 1 of this activity from 10-11am in the Walled Garden!

sessions.title: Metazooa: Live! Kickoff
sessions.description:
The viral daily biology game Metazooa comes to life in an immersive outdoor experience! Come to the Gardens to meet Abe, the founder of the indie game studio Trainwreck Labs, for the official kickoff of this weekend-long, nature-themed scavenger hunt. 

Learn more about the event here
https://metazooa.live

.

sessions.title: Crossword Editing 101
sessions.description: Crossword editors Quiara Vasquez and Natan Last will edit the winning crossword of the Megagame relay race live, and share notes on the editorial process with the audience.

sessions.title: Biddy Parts
sessions.description: Welcome to the Biddy Part Auction House, where mad scientists do their best to win the highest quality body parts to construct the most powerful abomination. Can you and your fellow scientists beat the other 5 teams while saving the most money. 6 teams of up to 5 scientists compete to win.

sessions.title: Election Tournament Conventions
sessions.description:
Three factions will enter the smoke-filled room. One will emerge as the Nominee of your party. How many parliamentary machinations and backroom deals will it take?

IMPORTANT: You don't technically have to, but it is strongly recommended to attend Stage 1 (10-11am in the Walled Garden), especially if you would like to be the Sovereign of Metagame. Stage 1 has more information about the overall election tournament!

sessions.title: Metazooa : Live! Finale
sessions.description: The resolution and debrief of your favorite on-going nature themed scavenger hunt

sessions.title: Nightmare High
sessions.description: For the entire summer you've woken up from a reoccurring nightmare you can barely remember. By the end of your first week of school, you and your entire after school club, will know exactly why you tried to forget. Nightmare High is a short 2 hour game made especially for teenagers in out of school time places or low socio-economic settings to engage them in the basic tenets of tabletop roleplaying games. Come play the short game, and engage in a conversation about designing for unique populations.

sessions.title: All-day Prototype Game Playing

sessions.title: Design Your 'Dead Man's Switch': Building Automation into ARG Design
sessions.description: What happens to your work if you're not around to finish it? In this workshop, you'll design your own disappearance protocol: a dead man's switch that activates upon your untimely departure. We'll craft encrypted messages, embed puzzle mechanics, and invent initiation rituals for those you'd trust to complete your Great Work to fidelity. Think of it as morbidly creative group therapy for our collective fear of being forgotten.

People of the world who pass on are called to the city to tell the story of their lives in this reflective, gentle, yet competitive card game.

Think Spirited Away meets Magic the Gathering, you make a deck of 15 cards to play against fellow players, winning rounds by making smart choices in how you play your cards.

sessions.description: Like checkers? Connect Four? Ches960?  Lost Cities? Abalone? Blokus? Why choose when you can have them all: with the board game round robin, you make one move, then move one seat over. This is the penultimate battle of the Megagame.

sessions.description:
Do you have what it takes to get elected Sovereign of Metagame? Help your team? Score points? Those goals may not align!

This activity has three stages:
Stage 1: Preliminary rounds, which may test your wit, negotiation abilities, and maybe even athleticism(?)
Stage 2: Purple and Orange Party Conventions, 1800s-style in a smoke-filled room
Stage 3: Dramatic debate & conference-wide election between the Purple and Orange Nominees — plus immediate inauguration of the Sovereign and their appointed Cabinet

sessions.description: Generunner is a two-player asymmetric deck-builder card game of biological warfare between phage and bacteria. Players play as phage or bacteria and utilize cards based off of real biological systems (restriction enzymes, methylation systems, CRISPR arrays, hypermutation, lysogeny, quantum sensing, etc) to evolve to beat their opponent.

sessions.title: Meta: the Game
sessions.description: This is the final round of the Megagame. Check your player's manual when you arrive for more information on what it'll include!

sessions.title: Kurt Vonnegut's GHQ: The Lost Board Game
sessions.description: GHQ is a 1v1 strategy game made by legendary author Kurt Vonnegut, based after his experiences of fighting in WWII. In this chess-like game, you manage infantry and artillery to capture the enemy HQ. Fast to learn, but lots of depth to strategies!

sessions.title: Jigsaw Speedsolving

sessions.title: Blood on the Clocktower

Find and kill the Demon lurking among you before the secret evil players destroy the town. Even if you are killed, you still play on as a ghost.

I've run almost 1000 new players through this game.

sessions.description: Like any other party, sex parties have default social dynamics which make them a less perfect version of what they could be. How do you design a game to incentivize behavior to make the party awesome? What's the right amount of rules to explain to a group of people waiting to take off their clothes?

sessions.description: Join us for Lovecraft Country: Dark Expeditions, a GM-less storytelling game powered by the Tableau system, where players collaboratively weave eerie tales of mystery and horror. Guided by the Tableau Accelerated Core Rules, we’ll venture into twilight journeys, tidal secrets, and creeping madness—facilitated by the game’s designer, Christopher Allen.

sessions.title: So You Want to be a Professional Game Developer — learn from my mistakes!
sessions.description:
Join us for a conversation between generations: between the burnt out husk who's been through it all, and the bright-eyed youth still filled with vigor. 

Lars is a former professional game developer, who made his own Indie one-hit wonder Defender's Quest, and was a collaborator on Dicey Dungeons, Friday Night Funkin', and many other titles.

Milo wants to achieve his own hopes and dreams, and Lars will do his best to tell Milo what Lars wishes he knew at his age.

sessions.title: Prompt Engineering, The Game: Cogs vs Clippies
sessions.description: A game that asks "what if your pieces had their own opinions?" In this session, we will playtest a collaborative game in which you deploy your Cogs to fight off waves of Clippies from the Friendly Paperclip Company. Your Cog is a Cooperative Open-ended Generative Systems: they decide what to do in the situation based on their prompt, the advice they've received from you and from other Cogs. Between rounds, we'll make tweaks to improve the interface and flow based on your feedback.

sessions.title: ​Video Games as Alignment Benchmarks: A Workshop
sessions.description: Multiplayer co-op games like Factorio, Overcooked, Left 4 Dead, and Minecraft have the ability to teach and measure skillfulness in strategic thinking and optimization. But even more importantly, they allow us to test the core organic alignment capability: role definition and role selection in dynamically evolving group contexts.  Game developers who have spent a lot of time thinking about what makes role choice interesting or difficult for human players, or who have experience with development of multiplayer games with roles, are especially encouraged to join.

sessions.title: TASK Party!
sessions.description: TASK Party is an improvisational community experience that follows a very simple structure of drawing a task to do from the TASK Box, completing said task in any style manner or interpretation, and then adding a task of your own back into the TASK Box. Beyond that, every task is up to your own interpretation - there is no failure or incorrect approaches, only losing yourself in the flow of experimentation and play. Trust us - it is more fun and less scary than it sounds and you will create things you would have never dreamed of otherwise.

sessions.title: Monsterhearts
sessions.description: Monsterhearts is a game about queer angsty teenage monsters, based on franchises like Buffy: The Vampire Slayer, Twilight, and the Craft. It uses the Powered By The Apocalypse engine, but the rules are very simple. This is a one-shot based extremely loosely on the movie The Breakfast Club.

sessions.title: Writing a Complete Horror One-Shot
sessions.description:
Horror is about the fear of the unknown, when the rules are unclear but the stakes are real. Come learn about building the structure of a self-contained spooky scenario, and how to precisely calibrate dread without drifting into action or comedy. 

We're following the Delta Green method for writing self-contained games, and you'll leave this workshop with a completed horror one-shot.

sessions.title: Murder Party
sessions.description: Bernard Billionaire invites you to his lavish mansion for one of his famous opulent parties to announce who will inherit his vast fortune. BUT WAIT! Someone just murdered Bernard, and it was one of the guests (maybe even you). Can you figure out who the murderer is while avoiding getting murdered yourself? Get murdered and become a ghost. Murder Party plays like a live action version of clue where you and the other 29 guests are all suspects.

sessions.title: Rulebooks: The good, the bad, and the incomprehensible
sessions.description: We'll look at several examples of exceptionally good rulebooks (Galaxy Trucker). Then, we'll look at a pair of exceptionally, legendarily bad rulebooks (Imperium: Legends and Imperium: Classics) and try to figure out 1) how to actually play the game, 2) how we could have written the rulebook better, and 3) compare our own attempt at a rules rewrite to Osprey's own revised "Imperium: Horizons" rulebook to see if our first draft is better than their revised draft.

sessions.title: Escape the Sudoku
sessions.description: Come play in this life-size sudoku + escape room experience from world sudoku champion Thomas Snyder where you'll need to work as a group to make everything follow the gamemaster's rules and earn your escape. (Game probably takes ~40 minutes; we are allowing for some setup and meet and greet time as well as running two instances if this reaches capacity.)

sessions.title: Sorcerority: A LARP
sessions.description:
Sorcerority is about the sisters (gender neutral) of a sorority (gender neutral) at a magic college, juggling room assignments and social drama.  The genre is modern fantasy, so street clothes are appropriate, but so are witch hats and anything else it would be fun to wear as a witch.  
This goes better with casting and reading ahead of time, so if you want to play, fill out a form at 
https://tinyurl.com/3c5kjvjv

(More public info about this LARP can be found at https://tinyurl.com/2s36j35z . This is a LARP for 10-11 players, so if 12 players are interested, one of the players will be on standby in case of a cancellation/illness.)

sessions.title: That Jazz Craze
sessions.description:
(Held in room 1D2 around the corner)
A Call of Cthulhu scenario set during the Harlem Renaissance, from the ENnie-awardwinning sourcebook Harlem Unbound. It's the dawn of the Jazz Age, but all the gramophone recordings so far have been by white artists. A musician from Harlem is trying to change that, but now he has disappeared under mysterious circumstances...

sessions.title: The Perfect HOST: A Jubensha Mystery
sessions.description:
The Perfect HOST is a jubensha mystery for 5-6 players (approximately 3 hours). 

All players have been assigned but spectators are eagerly welcomed to watch from the sidelines and solve the mystery themselves!

sessions.title: Ten Candles
sessions.description: Ten Candles is a zero-prep tabletop storytelling game designed for one-shot 2-4 hour sessions of tragic horror. It is best played with one GM and 3-5 players, by the light of ten tea light candles which provide atmosphere, act as a countdown timer for the game, and allow you to literally burn your character sheet away as you play. Ten Candles is described as a "tragic horror" game rather than survival horror for one main reason: in Ten Candles there are no survivors. In the final scene of the game, when only one candle remains, all of the characters will die. In this, Ten Candles is not a game about "winning" or beating the monsters. Instead, it is a game about what happens in the dark, and about those who try to survive within it. It is a game about being pushed to the brink of madness and despair, searching for hope in a hopeless world, and trying to do something meaningful with your final few hours left.
